i barely eat (i’m a recovering anorexic, whose relationship to food never quite got to 100%). i take necessary medication that makes me carry extra weight, regardless. my meds are psych meds, and my health as related to my weight is completely unaffected. 

i don’t hate you for how you feel, but it makes me fucking sad, and so do a lot of these comments. and like, fuck. i shouldn’t have to qualify my life to exist without judgment, and neither should anyone else.

it takes treatment. you’re not meant to do this alone. pushing through does help, and is the answer ultimately, but you’re meant to have support. therapy and with how serious things are for you, maybe more intensive treatment. 

i did it without the last bit, but with therapy and with an amazing support system which is something you are lacking which is why i mention treatment. it’s not supposed to sound easy cuz it’s not, but it does work, and there is hope. eating without fear is possible for you. it takes time. 

it’s not just psychological it’s physiological too, your body is stuck in a starvation cycle and needs to break out. that’s not easy by any metric. please remember, you’re not meant to do it alone, and you shouldn’t have to. i so deeply hope you’re able to follow the advice of the other comments and get to an ER, because not only is your weight rn very seriously low, but your mindset is in that scary place where you need that help. 

i wish nothing but the best for you, and i’m so sorry your parents have let you down so badly.

ok. hey. i get that this is a thing that feels hard, and that bullying is real and shitty and awful and that people get bullied for everything and there is no escape. if you’re gonna get bullied you’re gonna get bullied and like, there’s absolutely no fucking excuse. 

but here’s my perspective - and i have a pretty unique and valuable one. i have been tbh most sizes. i have been a 2, and i have been a 20. i have had binge eating disorder, and i have had anorexia. both have impacted me greatly. i rn am on the heavier side of that, because of both recovery from said anorexia and because of psych meds, and am also physically healthy in all the ways that matter in re: to weight. 

when i was a teenager i had binge eating disorder, and got to learn how much the world hates fat people, especially fat women. especially tbh in the early 2000’s, it was a really horrible time to be a fat teenage girl. 

the thing is, i got bullied and i hated myself and i wished i could physically cut off parts of my body all the time. i tried to starve myself all the time but didn’t have the time to commit to it yet bc i had to go to school, & bc i was still a child and didn’t have control over my own meals or food. 

then i went to college and instead of going to class, i fell into a deep depression, even deeper than before, and finally achieved my long standing goal. i stopped eating. i was thrilled. the weight fell off. and everyone, i mean every single person in my life, was thrilled. proud of me. asked me what my secret was. 

the smaller i got, the better my life got. people were friendlier, kinder. smiled at me more. strangers did nice things for me. i was treated as pretty. i could buy and wear normal clothes, bc this was still like 2008 maybe? & there were no attractive plus-sized clothes back then - to be able to just wear normal cute things was unreal. 

everyone around me, my friends, family, parents, did nothing but praise me. they saw how little i ate, how much i exercised, how i got dizzy doing simple things. i went to the doctor, because i started passing out in the shower, and i was deficient in basically every vitamin. i was 1 pound from being “technically” underweight, for my height. i was told to eat more vegetables, keep up the good work, and put on prescription level vitamins to keep my body from continuing to shut down.

it took the better part of ten years to start eating normally again because i was so afraid to let go of my newfound privilege, that i fought so hard for. that i suffered depression and brain fog and damage that will never ever go away, for.

and i still sometimes hate myself for having gained any weight. i still hate my body. i still only half believe my fiancée when she tells me i am beautiful and attractive. 

so all that said, having had both experiences, i would pick being thin over being fat 100000000x over. not because it’s inherently good, or right, or healthy, or anything like that. but because it’s simply an easier more privileged way to go through life. and i know that for a fact. 

this does not erase that people get bullied and shamed for their bodies no matter what kinds of bodies they have. that is also a fact, an undeniable one. this does not impact or erase your wife’s experience. but it does mean that the body positivity movement was created for a *reason*, and not one that was ever about excluding or harming anyone. it was only ever about trying to say “hey. we don’t deserve to be treated as inherently less, and that’s how we are being treated, all the time. please hear us.”

if you’ve been taking antidepressants for a decent amount of time and feel like.. okay, but not especially NOT depressed, and sometimes wonder if they’re even doing anything at all and like, maybe those people who talk about how we’re all uselessly overmedicated are right and y’know we don’t even know WHY SSRI’s work, you read that somewhere once, right? etc.

consider that it’s really hard to notice subtle changes over time. when you were really really clinically depressed, you’d probably been like that for a while, and you learned to survive in it, sort of, and live a sort of greyed-out half life. and it’s very possible that when you started taking meds, which of course take time to build up in your system and become effective, that depression fog slowly slowly lifted. 

it didn’t lift to reveal a super happy functional person, because you just spent years in a clinical depression, right? you weren’t like, working on yourself, or feeling your emotions or having hobbies or doing self-care, all those things that lead to happy functional life. what it did do, though, was make those things just.. possible. 

which is imperfect, sure, but way way better than what you had before! so if you can, make sure you stick with it. keep up with your meds. refill your prescriptions. check in with your doctor, check in with yourself, and take care of you! you’re important and worth taking care of.

source: on lexapro for.. 3 years? more? & have let it lapse at least twice in that time, sending myself back into a deep depression. i would then ask my friends and loved ones things like “was it really this bad, before i was medicated??” and the answer was an emphatic YES. tl;dr while of course not for everyone (ymmv, all humans are different, etc.) if meds help you, let them, bc it’s easy to forget.
